summary: Manipulate nodes via pointers instead of indices, using dummy heads and multi-pointer techniques (fast/slow, prev/curr) to reverse, merge, or detect structure in O(1) extra space.
recognize_when: Problem is phrased in terms of a singly or doubly linked list, not an array
You need to reverse, reorder, or splice nodes in place without extra storage
Cycle detection or finding the middle/kth-from-end node is required
Merging two or more sorted lists
In-place operations are required so an O(n) array conversion is disallowed

complexity.notes: A single pass (or two, for fast/slow techniques) with a constant number of pointers; no auxiliary array or hash map needed unless the variant requires one (e.g. cycle start with a hash set).

gotchas: Losing the reference to the rest of the list before reassigning next (always save next_node first)
Forgetting a dummy/sentinel head node when the result's head may change (e.g. merging, removing the first node)
Off-by-one when using fast/slow pointers to find the middle (decide up front whether you want the first or second middle for even-length lists)
examples: Remove Nth Node From End of List
